name: PT Surya Fajar Capital Tbk

frontmatter.title: Surya Fajar Capital — a licence and a cash pile do not make a franchise
frontmatter.summary: We maintain SELL. Surya Fajar Capital is a small advisory and fintech holding with falling revenue, losses to parent in every fiscal year, and shares priced at a book multiple the accounts do not support. The target values the cash-rich book at the peer median multiple. The negative return is the value gap, not a twelve-month forecast: we have no sourced, dated catalyst for it.
thesis: Revenue re-based onto the reported quarters is still a fraction of the FY2022A fee pool against a cost base built for a larger business, and every reported fiscal year has produced a loss to parent.
Earnings-based methods do not apply, because the return on equity is below the growth rate and no dividend can be paid; the only usable leg is the peer book multiple on the reported cash-rich book.
The shares trade at twenty-odd times reported parent book on a thin register, so the price reflects scarcity and flow rather than any earnings path we can source; the tape has not moved in a year.
Cash covers several years of the loss run-rate, so this is a slow erosion of book, not an imminent insolvency; the downside is the base-case arithmetic, and the upside risk is a control event.
The Q3 2026 jump in parent equity is mostly the minority interest moving into parent equity, not a large controller injection; we withdraw the earlier funding narrative.

catalysts.event: FY2026 audited financial statements, auditor opinion and any going-concern or capital-raise disclosure
Year-end OJK and IDX supervisory notices, including any unusual-market-activity letter
Annual general meeting — dividend, board changes and any rights issue or asset-injection approval

blocks.text: **What changed in this revision.** We maintain a **SELL** rating on PT Surya Fajar Capital Tbk (SFAN); the target is **Rp108** against a last price of **Rp1,950**, a total return of **-94.5%** [S0]. That return is the value gap at fundamental value (target plus nil dividend, against the price): it is not a forecast that the price reaches the target within twelve months, because we have no sourced, dated catalyst for the discount to narrow and give no probability that it does. The house rating rule reads the gap, so the rating is a statement of value. The red team found that the previous target was built wrongly, and we accept the main points. Three changes, in order of size. First, the blend: the earlier target carried the nil justified book-multiple leg and the nil dividend leg at half the weight and then took a further discount, which deleted half of the one usable value before the house liquidity rule applied. A nil leg is a method-fit failure, not a probability-weighted value, so the weight is now renormalised onto the usable leg, the peer book multiple of **1.6x** on the reported book, worth **Rp145** a share; the justified leg is kept at **5%** only because it is the industry's primary method and must stay in the printed table [S0]. Second, the cost of equity: the unlevered beta is back at the sector default, so the cost of equity is **11.9%**, the same as the sector's peers; the earlier higher beta had no fitted source. Third, the return on equity is rebased to the minority-nil loss run-rate and the equity basis is corrected (parent equity throughout, minorities separate). The peer median itself has fallen by more than a third since initiation as peer data packs refreshed, which moved the target before any of these changes. The house liquidity discount of **30%** is a mechanical rule keyed to traded value of **IDR90.9m** a day, not an analyst choice; the target before it is **Rp154** [S0].

**Against net cash.** The balance sheet at 30 September 2026 holds no borrowings and cash that is the majority of parent equity, and the red team's check was whether the target sits below net cash per share. It does not: the target is nearly twice net cash per share and a little above reported parent book per share, so we are not valuing the company below its cash [S0]. The previous target did sit below net cash, which we now regard as an error.

The company is a Jakarta-based financial holding with five reported segments: brokerage and underwriting, peer-to-peer lending, electronic payment services, securities crowdfunding and consultancy [S0][S6]. It was founded as a financial consultant, listed in 2019, and its lending subsidiary Indofund obtained its OJK licence in 2021 [S4][S6].

**The variant view** is not that the business is small. It is that the market values the equity as though the franchise were intact while the reported numbers show the opposite. Revenue fell from **IDR29.5bn** in FY2022A to **IDR1.2bn** in FY2024A, and the group reported a loss to parent in every fiscal year of our history: **IDR-17.0bn**, **IDR-20.7bn**, **IDR-14.2bn** and **IDR-47.6bn** [S0]. Parent equity fell from **IDR203.3bn** to **IDR126.3bn**, and the return on opening equity was **-25.1%** in the last audited year [S0]. Our model carries a loss of **IDR-17.7bn** in FY2025E (inferred, see the financial section) and **IDR-23.9bn** in FY2026E, with revenue of **IDR2.6bn** and **IDR5.3bn** in those years rising to **IDR5.8bn** in FY2027E [S0].

**What moves the value.** Not a commodity price or a demand cycle, but three things: whether the residual fee businesses cover a corporate cost base; how much book survives the next years of losses, which cash runway and the third-quarter cost line govern; and whether control changes hands or injects assets. A control event is the one path by which price and value could converge from above, and we treat it as the bull case in the risks section.

**Where the price sits.** At **Rp1,950** the shares trade at **21.0x** the FY2024A parent book per share of **92.9**, and at a similar multiple of the reported Q3 2026 parent book, which is the book the valuation uses [S0]. The justified book multiple, the correct primary method for a financial holding, is **-3.0** turns on a sustainable return of **-19.3%** and a cost of equity of **11.9%**, so it does not apply and is floored at nil [S0].

PT Surya Fajar Capital Tbk is an Indonesian financial-services holding company headquartered in Satrio Tower, Jakarta [S6]. It was founded as a financial consultancy in 2016 and listed in 2019 [S6]. The original proposition was transaction advice: mergers and acquisitions, divestitures, restructuring, and preparation for public offerings, rights issues and bond programmes [S6]. That is a mandate business; revenue arrives in lumps when deals close, the cost base is people and compliance, and the franchise is only as good as the pipeline in a given year.

The reporting structure spans five segments: brokerage and underwriter, financial-technology peer-to-peer lending, electronic payment services, technology with securities crowdfunding, and consultancy [S0]. The fintech leg has the documented regulatory milestone: PT Bursa Akselerasi Indonesia, trading as Indofund, obtained its OJK licence as an information-technology-based money-lending provider in August 2021 [S4]. That converted a consultancy into something with a recurring regulated activity, but the record shows the conversion did not produce a durable revenue base. Group revenue peaked at **IDR29.5bn** in FY2022A, fell to **IDR14.6bn** in FY2023A and **IDR1.2bn** in FY2024A [S0]. The pack then shows an erratic re-base: first and second quarter 2026 revenue was negative and the third quarter was positive and large, so the nine months to September 2026 already exceed the whole of FY2024A [S0]. We cannot tell from the pack whether the third quarter is a new level or a lumpy fee quarter, so we do not model it as either (see the financial section).

The group employed **111.0** people at the last count [S0]. For a company with revenue as small as this, that establishment is the core of the problem: a cost base sized for a diversified financial group against a boutique's revenue.

Ownership is concentrated. Insiders hold **73.7%** of the shares and the free float is **19.6%** [S0]. First, the traded price is set by a thin slice of the register, so it can sit far from value for a long time. Second, the controlling shareholders can approve capital raises, related-party transactions and strategy with little minority constraint. Both bear on valuation and governance.

The stock has drawn exchange attention before. In June 2023 the exchange placed SFAN on its unusual-market-activity list after a week in which the shares rose **8.5%** and closed at **Rp1,855/share** [S5]. A monitoring notice is not a finding of wrongdoing, but it documents the tape moving without a company disclosure.

Indonesia's securities-industry licences are granted and supervised by the financial services authority, and the capital-markets law gives the exchange a surveillance mandate that includes flagging trading patterns it considers outside normal behaviour. A monitoring notice is a signal about price formation, not a sanction. Readers should treat it as evidence about how this stock trades rather than as an allegation against the company.

SFAN sits at the intersection of three Indonesian financial industries: corporate-finance advice, brokerage and underwriting, and regulated digital lending [S0][S6]. All three are licensed, cyclical in fee income and crowded at the small end. Advice is fragmented among bank-affiliated houses, boutiques and accounting-firm arms, and mandates are won on relationships and balance-sheet capacity. Brokerage and underwriting need exchange membership and capital to absorb commitments. Digital lending is licensed, rate-capped and conduct-regulated, and competes with bank-backed platforms and large consumer-finance groups.

The competitive position is that of a very small challenger; the profile ranking tells us more about the number of listings than about franchise strength [S6]. Revenue in the last audited year was **IDR1.2bn** [S0], a scale at which fixed compliance, listing and audit costs are hard to cover. The strategy, as far as disclosures show, is to hold several small regulated permissions rather than build one durable franchise [S0]. A portfolio of small licences is an option-value argument, not an earnings argument, and we value it as such: through the peer book multiple, with no capitalised earnings.

The macro backdrop is supportive but not decisive. The house deck has Indonesian real GDP growth of **5.3** for FY2027E, inflation of **3.3** and a policy rate of **5.75** [S0]. A growing economy generates the corporate transactions and retail participation that feed these fee lines, but better-capitalised competitors take the mandates. Interest rates matter twice: a higher rate raises the cost of equity and compresses justified multiples, and the group's cash balance earns a market rate, which is a tangible support to the loss line. The deck's rupiah path of **18,225** spot against **18,350** for FY2027E implies continued currency pressure and higher-for-longer rates, which helps the cash and hurts the multiple [S0].

Regulation is the dominant external influence. The OJK's 2026 sanctions list records sanctions in the capital markets on parties other than SFAN, and no SFAN party appears in the excerpt we retrieved, so we make no allegation [S10]. The relevant point is that supervision is strict, a licence can be suspended, and a small operator has less capacity to absorb an interruption.

Five forces, plainly. Rivalry is high: advice mandates are contested by better-capitalised houses and lending by bank-backed platforms. Buyer power is high: corporate clients negotiate fees. Supplier power is moderate: licensed professionals and permissions are scarce but cannot be monopolised. New entrants are constrained by licensing but not blocked, least of all in advisory. Substitutes are real: private markets and bank debt substitute for public offerings and platform lending. None favours a sub-scale incumbent [S0].

There is no evidence of pricing power, switching costs in advisory, or a network effect at this scale in lending. What the group owns is a set of permissions, a name in a niche and a listing. A licence can be sold and a listed vehicle with financial licences has scarcity value in Indonesia, which is exactly why we do not value the equity at net cash alone; but option value is not a moat and it is not earnings [S0].

The macro regime is balance-of-payments pressure with a cautious stance on rate-sensitive Indonesian names, which is the category this equity falls into [S0]. The index and float changes of November 2026 do not name SFAN. For a stock with a free float of **19.6%**, a passive-index event would be a material flow catalyst in either direction; we monitor it and do not forecast it [S0].

**Evidence base.** The pack holds four fiscal years (FY2021A to FY2024A), two 2025 quarters (first and second) and three 2026 quarters, and no 2025 third or fourth quarter and no FY2025 annual. We searched the company's investor pages and the press for the FY2025 audited statements and the auditor's opinion and did not find them: the company pages carry navigation without documents [S2][S7][S8][S9], and the exchange's own site refuses automated retrieval by design. FY2025E in our model is therefore an inference from the reported equity roll, not a reported year, and we label it so. Every load-bearing financial figure here comes from the pack [S0]; we could not register a filing, and an owner drop of the FY2025 statements would be the first thing to close this gap.

**History.** Revenue was **IDR11.8bn** in FY2021A, **IDR29.5bn** in FY2022A, **IDR14.6bn** in FY2023A and **IDR1.2bn** in FY2024A, and the loss to parent was **IDR-17.0bn**, **IDR-20.7bn**, **IDR-14.2bn** and **IDR-47.6bn** [S0]. The FY2024A loss is the largest in the series on the smallest revenue: a fixed cost base meeting a collapsed fee pool. Gross profit was small, operating expenses were a large multiple of revenue, and the pack carries no impairment line, so it is an operating loss, not a write-off [S0]. Minorities absorbed part of it (**IDR-5.2bn**) [S0].

**Equity basis, reconciled.** The pack's equity line is parent equity throughout, and the minority interest sits in its own line: at FY2024A the pack shows parent equity of **IDR126.3bn** with a separate and substantial minority balance, and total assets less both leaves a liability figure consistent with the pack's current liabilities plus small non-current items, which is how we know the equity line excludes minorities [S0]. The earlier draft called the FY2024A line "total equity" and mixed bases; that was wrong. On one basis, parent equity ran from the FY2024A level down to roughly the first-quarter 2026 close plus that quarter's parent loss, which is our inferred opening 2026 book. Across the third quarter of 2026 two things happened together: the minority line went from a substantial balance to nil, and parent equity rose by a similar amount. Total equity (parent plus minority) was almost unchanged across the quarter while the group lost money, so most of the headline jump in parent equity is the minority interest moving into parent equity, through a buy-in or a deconsolidation, and only a modest remainder is a non-earnings increase whose source the pack does not name [S0]. We therefore withdraw the earlier "controller contribution" and "controller funding" language: it is not evidenced, and the remainder is too small to carry a funding thesis. Total assets and current liabilities also fell sharply in the quarter, which fits entities leaving the consolidation.

**Revenue.** FY2025E revenue of **IDR2.6bn** is the 2025 first half at its reported pace for the whole year, because no second half is in the pack. FY2026E of **IDR5.3bn** is the reported nine months plus a fourth quarter at the nine-month quarterly average. The earlier draft put the fourth quarter at a far lower figure and called the third quarter "one-off fee items"; nothing in the pack supports either, so we withdraw that wording and take the average, which treats the third quarter as neither a repeat nor a one-off. Thereafter fee income grows at a single-digit nominal rate to **IDR5.8bn** in FY2027E and **IDR7.0bn** in FY2030E, still a fraction of FY2022A [S0]. Revenue does not drive the equity roll in this template; the return on equity does.

**Profitability and the third-quarter cost line.** The return on opening equity is the only profitability line the template carries. FY2025E is **-14.0%**, inferred from the book roll between two reported balance sheets, not reported: no 2025 third or fourth quarter and no FY2025 annual statement is in the pack. The reported first-half 2025 parent loss, annualised on the FY2024A opening book, would be a return of a little over one-fifth negative, against about one-seventh negative for the book roll; the book roll therefore implies a second half running at under a third of the first-half pace, a gap the pack does not explain (part may be the minority share and other equity movements the roll does not separate). We let the book roll govern because it ties to two reported balances, whereas annualising the first half assumes a second half no filing shows. FY2025E does not feed the target, which applies the peer book multiple to the reported third-quarter 2026 book and floors the primary leg at nil, so the choice changes no valuation figure [S0]. FY2026E is **-22.0%**: the nine-month parent loss plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's total loss, because from the third quarter the minorities are nil and the whole loss falls on the parent [S0]. The group loss on a total basis was narrower in the second and third quarters than in the first, and the parent loss narrowed in the third quarter only because minorities were still booked a share in it. What did not improve is the cost line: third-quarter operating expenses were roughly double the second quarter's while revenue recovered, so the third-quarter result is better on revenue and worse on cost, and we do not read narrowing as a trend [S0]. We hold **-22.0%** from FY2027E to the end of the horizon: the minority-nil run-rate on the reported book is of the same order, so this is the last actual, not a forecast of improvement or deterioration. The rupiah loss falls from **IDR-23.9bn** to **IDR-3.3bn** in FY2034E only because the modelled book falls from **IDR84.7bn** to **IDR11.6bn**; the return is constant, so this is arithmetic, not a cost-cut forecast [S0].

**Rebasing the equity path.** The red team asked us to rebase the forecast book on the Q3 2026 balance sheet. The engine's template rolls equity from earnings only, and has no line for a reclassification of minority interests or other equity movements, so the modelled FY2026E book of **IDR84.7bn** sits well below the reported Q3 2026 parent book; we cannot change that without a filing-sourced restatement, which needs a reported FY2025 year we do not have. We have therefore removed the modelled book from everything that carries value: the valuation uses the reported Q3 2026 book directly, and the forecast multiples **24.4x** and **31.3x** in this report are on the modelled, earnings-only book and are therefore overstated against the reported book; the reported-book multiple is lower and is the one in the valuation section [S0].

**Cash, runway and cash flow.** The balance sheet at 30 September 2026 shows no borrowings and a cash balance that is the majority of parent equity [S0]. Cash at the last balance sheet covers roughly three to four years of the annualised nine-month operating outflow, and about three years of the minority-nil loss run-rate. On the third quarter's operating cash outflow alone it covers only about a year, but that quarter's outflow coincided with cash leaving with the deconsolidated entities (cash fell by more than the operating outflow while total assets fell by almost a quarter), so we do not annualise it [S0]. The runway is therefore a range, from about a year on the worst quarter to three or four years on the smoother measures, and it is the single most important number for the bear case; reported interest income on the cash partly offsets the burn. Capital expenditure is negligible and there is no dividend.

**Capital allocation.** With no free cash flow and no dividend, the allocative decisions are which subsidiaries to keep or sell and whether to accept more capital from the controller. The third-quarter changes (deconsolidation and minority buy-in) are the visible decision. Proceeds, terms and counterparties are not disclosed in anything we could register [S0]. **Group transactions, dated.** We registered press-feed headlines, not the IDX disclosures or article texts (idx.co.id refuses scripts and the feeds return titles only) [S13][S15]. They show: a March 2026 report that the company is selling **2.0 count** subsidiaries; an 18 August 2026 report that a group company is to take over a **52.0%** stake in PT DPI, that SFAN is to transfer all shares of Mitra Usaha Indofund, and that a subsidiary is to hold nearly all of Bursa Akselerasi Indonesia (the lending licence holder) [S13]. All three dates precede 30 September 2026. The headlines read as an intra-group reshuffle plus two disposals; the consideration, counterparties and completion dates are not evidenced. Completion within the third quarter is what the 30 September balance sheet looks like: the minority line is nil and total assets and current liabilities fell sharply [S0]. We therefore treat any cash received as already in the Q3 book, which the peer-book leg values through reported equity, and bridge nothing; adding a sale price would double-count. A consideration figure circulated in an earlier internal review is not in any registered source and is not used. Should a later disclosure show proceeds received after 30 September, they go into the valuation bridge with that source and the target is re-run.

**Earnings-quality flags, per the house card.** IDX board and notation status: we observe no special-monitoring-board designation and no notation letter in the pack or in any registered source, but the exchange's own announcements are not retrievable by design, so this is "not observed", not "confirmed clean" [S0][S5]. Accruals: operating cash flow was far better than the net loss in each of the last three fiscal years, so the accruals ratio is negative (non-cash charges and working capital, not earnings outrunning cash), the opposite of the manipulation signature [S0]. Receivables are not outgrowing revenue because revenue is not growing. Provisioning against write-offs for the lending book cannot be run: the pack has no loan-book, provisioning or write-off line, so we record it as unavailable, not zero. Related-party flows as a share of revenue and assets: not disclosed in the pack or in anything registered, so unquantified. Going-concern status and auditor opinion: not found (above); this is a gap in our evidence. Structure flags: a concentrated register with a thin float; the Q3 2026 deconsolidation and minority buy-in, whose terms and counterparties are undisclosed and which is the sort of step that can precede an asset injection or a related-party transaction; a share count that has never changed; and the 2023 exchange monitoring notice [S0][S5]. We found no fabricated cash and no fictitious revenue; all flags are optics-class or structure-class, and we class the minority transaction as structure-class pending disclosure.

**Method fit.** This is a financial holding with negative earnings in every history and forecast year, no dividend, and a book that is mostly cash. The industry's primary method, justified price-to-book, expresses value as the return on equity relative to the cost of equity: a business earning below its cost of capital is worth less than book. Here the return is negative, so the formula gives a negative multiple at any plausible cost of equity, and the engine floors the value at nil [S0]. That floor is a limited-liability convention; for a company holding net cash it understates, because a holder could in principle liquidate to cash. P/E needs positive earnings and the dividend model needs a dividend, so both fail. Three of the three earnings-based methods therefore do not apply, which is a method-fit finding about the company, not a probability-weighted zero. The one usable leg is the peer book multiple, and we say plainly that it is a market convention and not a franchise valuation.

The cost of equity is the engine's published build: a risk-free rate of **7.4%**, less the house default spread of **1.6%**, plus an unlevered beta of **0.90** (the sector default) times the sum of the mature premium of **4.2%** and the country premium of **2.5%**, which is **11.9%** [S0]. A financial company is treated as equity-financed, so the cost of capital equals the cost of equity. The earlier higher beta had no fitted source and is withdrawn.

The primary leg produces **-3.0** turns of book on a sustainable return of **-19.3%**, a cost of equity of **11.9%** and terminal growth of **4.0%**, floored at nil [S0]. We keep it in the blend at **5%**, the smallest weight that keeps the primary in the printed table, so that the reader sees the nil rather than a silent omission; it moves the value by that weight, not by half.

**The peer leg and the peer list.** The peer set is every company in the industry master's FINANCIAL_HOLDCOS group with a defined trailing price-to-book from its own data pack, after SFAN is removed. The table below lists each peer and the multiple used, so the median reproduces: it is **1.6x** on trailing price to reported book, applied to SFAN's reported Q3 2026 parent book to give **Rp145** a share [S0].

A second, different number exists and the two should not be confused: the division's cross-company comparison table shows peer multiples struck on each peer's first forecast-year modelled book, whose median is higher; that is a forecast-book basis and is not comparable with a reported-book leg, so the engine uses the trailing basis, which is also the basis on which SFAN's own multiple is quoted. If instead one used the higher forecast-basis median, the target would be about a sixth higher than ours and the SELL would not change. We do not screen for return on equity or size: almost none of the peers would survive an ROE screen, and SFAN would fail any screen it imposed. The leg is generous to a loss-maker, because its peers carry positive returns on average and SFAN's return is negative. The sensitivity to composition is large: on the trailing basis three names in the set (a securities house and two holding companies) trade at several times book for reasons unrelated to SFAN, and excluding them would cut the median by more than half, to well below book; on the forecast basis the same exclusion cuts it by more than a third. We disclose both and apply neither, because the full-universe median is the reproducible rule.

This leg is an equity value, not an enterprise value. Net cash does not enter it twice: the multiple is applied to reported parent equity, which already contains the cash, and the bridge line printed in the model output is not deducted [S0]. Cash is the majority of the book, so the honest reading is a market multiple on a cash-heavy, fee-light shell.

**The target stack.** The blend is **95%** the peer leg and **5%** the nil primary, giving a fundamental value of **Rp138** a share. Rolled forward one year at the cost of equity it gives **Rp154**, and after the house liquidity discount of **30%**, which the fund's limits apply to every name whose average daily traded value is below the lowest liquidity threshold (here **IDR90.9m**), the target is **Rp108**, a total return of **-94.5%** [S0]. We do not control that discount and have not tuned it; it applies to the fundamental value, not to the market price, and it reflects what a buyer of a whole position would pay. We checked the stack against net cash: the target is a multiple of net cash per share and a little above reported book per share, so it is not a value below cash. Under the industry-default weights the blend would be nil, because two of its three legs do not exist for SFAN; so the stack we show is not a cautious layering but the removal of a mechanical zero.

**Divergence.** The primary says nil because the franchise earns a negative return; the cross-check says a fraction of the price because the market pays a book multiple for anything with a financial licence. The blend is a compromise between an accounting truth and a market convention. If the group ever shows a positive return above the growth rate, the primary switches on and the target rises quickly; until then the peer leg is what holds the target above net cash.

**Sensitivity.** The sensitivity table below covers return on equity and cost of equity; because the primary is floored across most of the grid it is flat, then jumps when the return crosses the growth rate. The sensitivity that matters is to the peer multiple, which moves the value one-for-one: a fifth lower multiple takes a fifth off the peer leg and leaves the target above net cash per share; a multiple at about half the median would put it at about net cash, and the lower-quartile peers trade well below that. The engine's scenario switch cannot move a market multiple (see the scenario discussion below), so we state this here in prose and not in the table.

**What the price implies.** At **Rp1,950** the shares trade at about twenty-one times reported parent book per share. On the justified formula that requires a sustainable return on equity of about one and two-thirds times book value every year, because the multiple equals the return less growth over the cost of equity less growth; the reverse-valuation routine in the engine cannot bracket the price within any sensible return, which is the same finding [S0]. The market is therefore not discounting a higher earnings path than ours; it is pricing something other than earnings. The only profit to parent we can source is a single 2021 first quarter, which is not a run-rate [S4]. With a free float of **19.6%** and insider ownership of **73.7%** [S0], the most likely explanation is scarcity of supply on a thin register plus an option on a control event. That is a reason to be careful about expressing a short view, as much as a reason not to be long.

**Franchise risk (we are wrong about the business).** If the residual advisory and lending businesses have a pipeline the disclosures do not show, revenue could recover faster than modelled and the return could improve. We would see it first in the fee line and operating cash flow. The effect on our target is small by construction, because the primary leg is floored and the peer leg is struck on reported book; this is a limitation of the method and we say so. Likelihood medium, impact on a positive return low in our target but high on the price.

**Cash runway and funding.** The runway is a range, from about a year on the worst quarter to three or four years on the smoother measures (see the financial section). The controller can fund a shortfall, but we no longer say it has: the Q3 2026 equity jump is mostly the minority interest moving into parent equity. A capital raise at **Rp1,950** would be accretive to book per share, not dilutive, because the shares trade far above book, so the cost of a raise falls on whoever does not take part and on the terms of any related-party subscriber; that is a governance risk, not a share-count risk. Likelihood medium, impact on the bear case high.

**Cost line.** Third-quarter operating expenses roughly doubled against the second quarter. If that is the new base, the loss run-rate is larger than the rate we hold, the book falls faster and the runway shortens; if it is restructuring cost, the run-rate improves. We cannot tell from the pack and hold the minority-nil run-rate. Likelihood medium, impact medium.

**Peer de-rating.** The peer leg moves one-for-one with the median multiple, which depends on a small set that includes a few names trading at many times book. A de-rating to about half the median would take the target to about net cash, and toward the lower-quartile peers the mechanical target would fall below net cash. Likelihood medium, impact high, and the engine's scenario table cannot show it.

**Supervisory and regulatory.** The value rests on licences, and a licence can be suspended or revoked. The OJK's 2026 sanctions list shows active enforcement in the capital markets, none against SFAN in the excerpt we retrieved [S10]. We draw no inference about SFAN from other companies' cases. Likelihood low, impact high.

**Liquidity and market.** The shares trade at **Rp1,950** inside a fifty-two-week range of **Rp1,900** to **Rp2,050**, on **IDR90.9m** a day and a **19.6%** float with no institutional holders [S0]. Our expected return assumes convergence to fundamental value; the tape has not converged for a year, and no dated catalyst forces it. A short expression carries borrow and squeeze risk our target does not capture. Likelihood high, impact high on timing.

**Rates and currency.** The deck has the policy rate at **5.75** and the rupiah at **18,225** spot [S0]. A higher cost of equity lowers justified multiples and a weaker rupiah raises imported technology and compliance costs. Likelihood medium, impact low.

Small licensed financial firms in emerging markets typically survive on a combination of fee income and shareholder support, and the failure mode is rarely a sudden insolvency. It is a slow erosion of capital in which the licence is retained, the listing is retained, and the equity value migrates to whoever funds the next recapitalisation. That pattern is worth keeping in mind when reading the scenarios below: the bear case is not a collapse, it is a transfer.

**Scenarios.** The table below shows the three operating scenarios, with mirrored shocks to the return on equity and probabilities of a quarter, a half and a quarter. Bear and bull print the same target as base, and we say why: the engine's scenario switch shifts model inputs, not the peer multiple or the reported balance sheet, and the only input-driven leg (the primary) is floored at nil in all three cases. The tails move the book path and the forecast multiples, but not the rupiah target. We do not hide this behind a distorted shock; we describe the value-relevant cases here instead.

**Read this table for what it is.** The three scenarios print the same value because the engine's scenario levers are inputs, driver decks and the cost of equity, and the value here rests on the peer book multiple applied to the reported book, which none of them touches; the return-on-equity shock moves only the nil primary leg. The probabilities therefore carry no value information in this table and we do not quote a probability-weighted value. A mirrored peer-multiple shock (a fifth lower and a fifth higher) is not available in the engine; its effect is one-for-one on the peer leg, which is **95%** of the blend, as the sensitivity discussion in the valuation section says. The bull path (net cash plus an injected business plus a listing premium) is valued at nil in the table: no registered source gives an injection, its size or a premium, so any figure would be invented. The bear and bull paragraphs below are descriptions, not valued outcomes.

*Bear (value).* The peer multiple falls toward the lower-quartile peers, or the third-quarter cost line proves to be the base, or both. The mechanical target falls to about net cash per share or below; for a shell we would take net cash less the burn expected before any exit as the floor-like value, and it is far below the price. The runway is then the binding variable.
*Base.* The 2026 minority-nil run-rate persists, the peer median holds, and book erodes slowly with cash covering the loss for several years; the target is the one in this report.

*Bull (value).* A control event: the Q3 2026 deconsolidation and minority buy-in are the kind of step that can precede an asset injection into a listed shell, which on the Indonesian exchange carries a scarcity value we do not deny. In that case the equity is worth net cash plus whatever the injected business is worth plus a listing premium, and the peer multiple on a larger book would be the measure. Nothing in the pack or in any registered source evidences such a plan, and we put it in the bull case, not the base. Revenue in the third quarter was positive and large and the parent loss narrowed from the first quarter, which is consistent with a restructuring but, as the financial section explains, the narrowing is mostly the disappearance of the minority share.

**What the negative return means, and what it does not.** The house target is fundamental value rolled one year, not a forecast of the tape, and the negative total return is the value gap, not a twelve-month price call. The holdco method card asks for a named, dated catalyst for a discount to narrow; for a premium to value to close we have none, and we give no probability that the price reaches the target within twelve months. The dated items we monitor (the FY2026 audited statements, year-end supervisory notices, the 2027 AGM) are information events, not convergence catalysts. The rating is therefore a statement of value, and an investor should not read it as a timed short. For konglo-group and high-concentration names the division has a regime overlay that prices how much of a premium persists, and SFAN is neither: the division's registry shows it as neither a konglo-group member nor a high-shareholder-concentration name, and its free float is above the exchange minimum. On our evidence the tape's last twelve months, pinned in a narrow range, is the strongest argument against convergence in any given year, and we state it as the main risk to the timing of the call. We are not forecasting a collapse in the quoted price within twelve months. We are saying the price is far above any value we can source, the gap is the base-case arithmetic, and the rating is a statement of value, with a high probability that the price stays high for longer than the arithmetic suggests.

**Signposts that would change our view.** A full-year positive return on equity, the only thing that unfreezes the primary leg; a disclosed transaction or asset injection at a valuation above book, which would fix the multiple leg; a capital raise or further controller contribution, which we would read through its terms; a disclosed mandate pipeline; the FY2026 auditor's opinion and any going-concern emphasis. Conversely, a fourth quarter that repeats the third quarter's cost line, or a supervisory action against a group entity, would push toward the bear case.

Ownership is concentrated and the float is thin. Insiders hold **73.7%** and institutions **0.0%**, leaving a free float of **19.6%** [S0]. The controlling group dominates the register, so the decisions that matter (divestments, capital raises, related-party transactions, board composition) are taken without meaningful minority participation. The profile data name a president director, a head of finance and a corporate secretary [S0]; we could not retrieve a board list, committee composition or independence statement, because the company's investor page carried no documents [S2].

The dividend record is unambiguous: none in any year of the price history and none in our forecast [S0]. A company that never distributes and whose equity is falling offers the minority holder nothing except a sale or a turnaround.

Related-party risk is the modal value-destruction channel on this exchange, and we could not quantify it: the pack does not disclose related-party revenue or balances, the company site did not serve its statements [S2], and no registered source quantifies flows to affiliates [S4][S5]. We report it unquantified, not absent. The Q3 2026 minority buy-in or deconsolidation is a related-party question until its terms are disclosed.

Structure flags per the house card: a concentrated register with a small float; documented exchange monitoring of price behaviour in 2023, with the shares up **8.5%** in a week and closing at **Rp1,855/share** [S5]; a share count that has never changed, so any raise would be the first dilution in the visible record; and subsidiaries that carried minority shareholders and were then deconsolidated or bought in, a structure we want documented [S0]. They are optics-class and structure-class flags; none is a manipulation-class flag on the evidence we hold.

The auditor and the opinion on FY2025 are not in our sources, and neither is a going-concern statement. We asked for the annual report and investor documents and were served navigation pages [S2][S7][S8][S9]; the exchange's own site is closed to automated retrieval. The gap is in our evidence, not necessarily in the company's disclosure. It is the first thing to close, by an owner drop of the FY2025 statements.

ESG exposures are specific and modest in scale. The direct environmental footprint is an office and a technology stack, so the environmental question is indirect: borrowers' exposure through the lending book and payment-fraud and data-protection risk. Social risk sits in conduct: retail lending under rate caps, collections and complaints. Governance is where the exposure actually is: a concentrated register, a thin float, no dividend, limited public disclosure and a listed vehicle whose value rests on licences rather than operations [S0].

The dated catalysts are in the frontmatter. The FY2026 audited statements, due by the end of the first quarter of 2027, settle the questions that matter: the run-rate, the auditor's view on going concern, and the terms of the Q3 2026 equity movements [S0]. The annual general meeting is the forum for any rights issue, dividend or board change [S2]. Year-end supervisory notices are the third dated item, because a monitoring letter or licensing action can move a thin float [S5][S10].

Between those dates we watch: the quarterly fee line against our revenue path; the operating expense line against the third quarter's level; operating cash flow and the cash balance, which give the runway; parent equity and book per share, the denominator of the valuation; the minority line (any reappearance); the share count, because any change is dilution; and traded value and free float, which feed the liquidity discount [S0]. We also monitor the regulatory register and exchange notices for any action naming a group entity, and the company's investor page for the first time it serves a statement [S2].

The honest summary is that the evidence is thin. We hold the data pack, one licensing news record, one exchange notice, a profile page and an enforcement list [S0][S4][S5][S6][S10]. We do not hold the annual report, the FY2025 statements, a board list, the auditor's opinion or a related-party note. Those gaps do not change the direction of the call, since a business with a negative return on equity, no dividend and a book multiple above twenty is expensive on any reading, but they do limit the precision of the target. If a filing shows a fee base recovering faster than the pack implies, or an asset injection, we will say so and move the estimate.

bear.narrative: Mirrored operating shock: the return on opening equity is six points worse than base, i.e. the third-quarter opex of 12.8 persists with no fee recovery, so the book is consumed faster and the controller has to fund more. The scenario switch moves inputs, not the peer multiple or the reported balance sheet (the engine's scenario levers are inputs, decks and the cost of equity, not a peer multiple), so the rupiah target is the same in all three cases and the probabilities carry no value information here; the de-rating and runway effects are described in section 5 outside the table, unvalued because no sourced figure exists.

bull.narrative: Mirrored operating shock: the return on opening equity is six points better than base, i.e. the loss narrows to roughly the 2025 first-half rate on a lower cost base after the 2026 deconsolidations. The return stays far below the cost of equity, and the peer multiple on the reported book is unchanged by the switch, so the rupiah target is the same. The shell and scarcity value that could lift it (net cash plus an injected business plus a listing premium) is valued at nil in the table because no registered source gives an injection, its size or a premium; it is described in section 5 and carries no probability-weighted value.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs ROE and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Rebased on the reported quarterly series, not on the collapsed FY2024A base alone. The pack has 2025 first-quarter revenue 1.52 and second quarter -0.21 (first half 1.31), and 2026 first quarter -1.27, second quarter -0.73 and third quarter +5.96 (nine months 3.97); there is no 2025 third or fourth quarter in the pack. FY2025E is the 2025 first half at its actual pace for the full year, 2.62 (modelled 2.58 = FY2024A 1.17 x 2.20). FY2026E is the reported nine months plus a fourth quarter at the nine-month quarterly average (3.97 / 3 = 1.32), i.e. about 5.29, +105% on FY2025E. The earlier version put the fourth quarter at 0.66 (the 2025 half-year average), below the third quarter's 5.96 with no source for the drop; the nine-month average treats the third quarter as neither a repeat nor a one-off, because the pack does not say which it is (the earlier 'one-off fee items' wording was an unsourced assumption and is withdrawn). Thereafter the fee pool grows 10%, 8%, 6% then 5% nominal because no disclosure evidences a return to the FY2022A level (29.5). Revenue does not drive the equity roll in this template; the return on equity does [S0].

assumptions.label: ROE on opening equity
assumptions.basis: Equity here is PARENT equity throughout: the pack's equity line excludes the minority interest, which sits in the separate minority_bs line (FY2024A: parent 126.31, minority 32.37; assets 178.96 less both leaves 20.3 of liabilities, matching the 16.2 of current liabilities). FY2025E -0.14 is inferred, not reported: the pack has no 2025 third or fourth quarter and no FY2025 annual, so we read it off the opening 2026 parent equity, which is the 2026 first-quarter close of 99.07 plus that quarter's parent loss of 9.41 = 108.5; against 126.31 at FY2024A that is -14.1%. FY2026E -0.22: the nine-month 2026 parent loss is 17.34 (9.41 + 4.51 + 3.42), and from the third quarter the minorities are nil, so the fourth quarter's loss falls entirely on the parent at the third quarter's total loss of 6.71 (the third quarter booked a further 3.29 to minorities that no longer exist at 30 September); 17.34 + 6.71 = 24.05 on the engine's opening 108.6 = -22.1%. The same -0.22 is held flat for later years: it is the minority-nil run-rate (6.71 x 4 = 26.8 on the reported 125.88 book is -21%), the last actual, and no later year improves or worsens. Because the engine rolls equity from earnings only, the modelled book sits below the reported 125.88 (the template has no line for the third-quarter reclassification of minority interests into parent equity or for the other equity increase described in the share_change basis), so the rupiah loss on the modelled book falls over time; that is arithmetic of the template, not a cost-cut forecast. The valuation does not use this path: the P/B leg uses the reported 2026Q3 book [S0].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2025E 0.10: the 2025 first half booked 1.80 of a 15.37 total loss to minorities (11.7%). FY2026E 0.22: the nine months booked 6.74 of a 24.1 total loss to minorities (28%), and the fourth quarter none, so the full-year share is about 6.74 / 30.8 = 22%. From FY2027E nil: the 30 September 2026 balance sheet shows minority_bs at 0.0007 against 27.96 at 30 June [S0].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Nil. SFAN has paid no dividend in any year in the price history and has accumulated losses; no disclosed restructuring step returns cash to parent shareholders [S0].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: The share count is 1,359.9m in every period of the pack, including 2026Q3. Parent equity rose 30.4 in 2026Q3 (95.52 to 125.88) while minority_bs fell 27.96 to nil: total equity (parent plus minority) moved from 123.48 to 125.88, +2.40, against a total loss of 6.71, so about 9.1 of the quarter's equity change is neither earnings nor a visible minority reclassification (a capital contribution, a gain on deconsolidation or a buy-in below carrying value; the pack does not say which). The earlier 'about Rp30bn controller contribution' was wrong: about 28 of the 30 is the minority interest moving into parent equity. No new shares, so the count is held flat [S0].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth
assumptions.basis: The house IDR nominal anchor of 4%; it only matters to the justified-P/B formula, which is negative at any defensible growth rate for a business whose return on equity is below it [S0].
